title: Sort by Length
statement:
Sort a list of words from shortest to longest with your language's built-in sort. Words of the same length go in alphabetical order.

The input is one line of lowercase words separated by single spaces. There is at least one word, and a word can appear more than once. Print the sorted words on one line, separated by single spaces.

Input:

```text
pear fig banana kiwi apple
```

Expected output:

```text
fig kiwi pear apple banana
```
hints: You do not need to write a sorting algorithm. The standard sort accepts a key function or a comparator that decides the order.
Compare lengths first. Only when two lengths are equal, compare the words themselves.
